question: Twelve email subject lines each go to 50 people. The best opens at 30%, against the usual 20%. What should the firm do next?
options: Run that one again on its own
answer: Run it again on its own. On 50 sends, a line that truly opens at 20% can land anywhere from about 10% to 30% by luck, so the best of twelve is also the luckiest of twelve. Retested alone, a winner picked that way usually slides back to the pack.
move: The winner of a big search has to win again to count.
ask: What big win after a wide search have I not yet tried to repeat?
trap: Use it everywhere, since 30% plainly beats 20%.

notes: 50 each: the best of 12 lines opens at 30%, the original at 20%. All 12 are truly 20%.
500 each: 23% against 21%. Most of the lead was luck.
5,000 each: 20% and 20%. The winner is an ordinary line.
50,000 each: still 20% and 20%. It was picked for its luck, not its words.

reference: Kohavi, Tang & Xu, Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments, Cambridge University Press, 2020
